appraisal_events.evidence: "Cela me fait plaisir parce que c'est un homme de talent." ... "il sera beaucoup pardonné à Bergotte puisqu'il a trouvé mon petit enfant gentil."
appraisal_events.explanation: The mother rehabilitates Bergotte, praising his talent and explicitly forgiving his faults because he praised the narrator; the father's earlier charge of a false, malicious character visibly loses its grip, unable to withstand the flattery.

appraisal_events.evidence: "M. de Norpois est tout ce qu'il y a de plus gentil, mais il n'est pas toujours très bienveillant, surtout pour les gens qui ne sont pas de son bord." -- "C'est vrai, je l'avais aussi remarqué", répondit mon père.
appraisal_events.explanation: The mother questions Norpois's fairness, suggesting his judgments are biased against those outside his circle, and the father concurs, denting Norpois's credibility as an impartial authority.

status_effects.explanation: Bergotte moves from open family condemnation to enthusiastic, explicit pardon and praise within this passage.
Norpois's reputation for fairness is locally dented when both parents agree he can be ungenerous toward those not of his own set.
